b1.note: Confirmed current on MDN and web.dev: a document must send COOP: same-origin plus COEP: require-corp (or credentialless), and not be blocked by Permissions-Policy cross-origin-isolated, to get SharedArrayBuffer. This applies across Chrome/Edge, Firefox (since FF79), and Safari.

b2.note: timestamp-query is a standard optional GPUFeature requestable via requestDevice({requiredFeatures:['timestamp-query']}) without any unsafe/dev flag in current stable Chrome; results are quantized to ~100µs resolution for timing-attack mitigation unless the WebGPU Developer Features flag is enabled to disable quantization.

b3.verdict: disagree: module-level validation/compilation of a Wasm module that declares shared memory does not itself require cross-origin isolation — WebAssembly.validate()/compile() succeed regardless. What actually fails without cross-origin isolation is runtime use: you cannot construct/receive a SharedArrayBuffer, so the module can't actually be instantiated with real multi-agent shared memory/threads.
b3.note: The gating mechanism is postMessage()/construction of SharedArrayBuffer throwing outside a cross-origin-isolated context, not module validation.

rows.claim: Yes: a cross-origin iframe can obtain cross-origin isolation if the parent adds allow="cross-origin-isolated" and either the iframe sends its own COOP+COEP(require-corp)/CORP headers, or the parent uses COEP: credentialless (Chrome ≥96) to avoid needing subresource cooperation; Chrome 137+ additionally offers Document-Isolation-Policy for simpler per-frame isolation without a full-page COEP rollout.
rows.verifier_hint: developer.chrome.com/blog/document-isolation-policy; web.dev cross-origin-isolation-guide

rows.claim: Yes via the standard mechanism (iframe allow="cross-origin-isolated" plus the iframe's own COOP/COEP/CORP headers); COEP: credentialless is also supported in Firefox, easing third-party embedding, but Firefox has no Document-Isolation-Policy equivalent.
rows.verifier_hint: MDN Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy browser-compat table

rows.claim: The standard iframe allow="cross-origin-isolated" + iframe's-own-headers path should work per spec, but COEP: credentialless / iframe-credentialless appear to be Chromium-only per one source, meaning Safari likely lacks the easier opt-in path and would need full CORP cooperation from the embedded origin.
rows.verifier_hint: MDN Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy browser-compat table; WebKit feature status page
rows.notes: Lower confidence — not independently confirmed against a WebKit-authored source this session.
